title: Practitioner reporting of controlled substance theft or significant loss
rule_summary: The registrant shall notify the Field Division Office of the Administration in his area, in writing, of the theft or significant loss of any controlled substances within one business day of discovery of such loss or theft, and must also file a complete and accurate DEA Form 106 with the Administration through DEA's Diversion Control Division secure network application within 45 days after discovery of the theft or loss. In determining whether a loss is significant a registrant should consider, among others, the actual quantity lost in relation to the type of business; the specific controlled substances lost; whether the loss can be associated with access by specific individuals or attributed to unique activities; a pattern of losses over a specific time period, whether the losses appear random, and the results of efforts taken to resolve them; and, if known, whether the substances are likely candidates for diversion and local trends and other indicators of diversion potential. Where a retail pharmacy contracts with private, common or contract carriers to retrieve filled prescriptions from a central fill pharmacy, the retail pharmacy is responsible for reporting in-transit losses upon discovery by use of a DEA Form 106.
exam_relevance: Tests whether the candidate applies the practitioner paragraph to a pharmacy rather than the non-practitioner paragraph, and can state both clocks and the significance factors.

numeric_facts.fact: written notice of theft or significant loss to the DEA Field Division Office
numeric_facts.conditions: from discovery of the loss or theft

numeric_facts.fact: filing of DEA Form 106 through the secure network application
numeric_facts.conditions: after discovery of the theft or loss

common_confusions: A pharmacy is a practitioner, so its theft or loss duty sits in 21 CFR 1301.76(b) and not in the non-practitioner paragraph 21 CFR 1301.74(c).
The in-transit allocation in 21 CFR 1301.76(d) puts the duty on the pharmacy that contracted the carrier, which is the opposite direction from the supplier allocation in 21 CFR 1301.74(c).
verification_notes: Read in the current eCFR text of 21 CFR 1301.76(b) and (d) on ecfr.gov on 2026-09-11. Added as a new rule so that no released adjudication is disturbed. A fresh independent audit is still required before any section relying on it is published.
